reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the proposal is consistent with that: the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs and no comment is emitted, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited evidence supports the conclusion. Section 13.6 (p0117) affirmatively preserves each party's right to independently develop, and 14.8 (p0131) confirms Corio solely directs and may subcontract the Corio Services — neither imposes a covenant not to build, buy or resell competing e-procurement products.

The 'CORIO MARKET SEGMENT' (p0013) and 'TERRITORY' (p0024) constructs are drafted as the scope of the licenses granted to us ('the area in which the licenses granted herein are applicable'), not as covenants restricting the businesses we may operate; license field-of-use/territory scope of this kind does not bar us from sourcing or developing competing products, so treating them as non-triggering is defensible.

Deterministic check ('no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains') passes, and the rationale correctly notes there is no surviving post-term restraint and that Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding.

Minor note for the record (not a basis to fail): the Market Segment revenue cap and North America territory operate as practical commercial limits on where we can deploy this Software, so if the license grant language elsewhere converts them into an affirmative covenant not to serve larger or ex-North America customers, the rule would need to be re-evaluated as a deviation.
